title: Drums, mellophone and tuba before the bass took over
summary: Garland corrects the books: he played drums in brass bands at twelve or thirteen, then mellophone, with Black Benny, and tuba only in California around 1925.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: No. That was in New Orleans.
I didn't play tuba until I came out here.
I was out here, I started to playing that tuba. I got -- that was about '25. (Unintelligible)
Right after I made that record. The first record that we made, about '23, '22 or '23, something like that. And I started playing the tuba.

Okay. Because some of the books say that you started with the drums, as we were talking earlier, and then say switched to tuba and mellophone in your teens, and were playing marching gigs and then went to the bass. So let's get all that straightened out now.
No, they start from the drums. They say I played drums.
I did play drums. I played the drums. I used to be the drummer in the bands, the brass bands. We'd have brass bands, you know?
You know, carnivals, and whenever somebody would die, them boys on the corner would collect the money, you know, to pay play for the band.
And give you a band, you understand.
How old were you now, when you were playing drums in these bands?
Oh, I was 12 or 13 years old.
Okay. And you were playing the bass at nine, so you --
Then I picked up on the mellophone, which we called alto --
I used to do that in the band.
And we had Benny -- put Benny to play
it. A fellow they called Black Benny.
Oh. Was he the bass drum player?
He could play the drums, yeah, very good, too.
